speaker: Moderator
text: Good evening, Mr. President, Senator Kerry.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Yes, I do.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. President, you have a 90-second rebuttal.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I, too, thank the University of Miami, and say our prayers are with the good people of this state, who’ve suffered a lot.

speaker: Moderator
text: New question, Mr. President, two minutes.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: No, I don’t believe it’s going to happen. I believe I’m going to win, because the American people know I know how to lead. I’ve shown the American people I know how to lead.

speaker: Moderator
text: Ninety second response, Senator Kerry.

speaker: John Kerry
text: I believe in being strong and resolute and determined. And I will hunt down and kill the terrorists, wherever they are.

speaker: Moderator
text: New question, two minutes, Senator Kerry.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Well, where do you want me to begin?

speaker: Moderator
text: Ninety-second response, Mr. President.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: My opponent looked at the same intelligence I looked at and declared in 2002 that Saddam Hussein was a grave threat.

speaker: Moderator
text: New question, Mr. President. Two minutes.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Jim, we’ve got the capability of doing both.

speaker: Moderator
text: Senator Kerry, 90 seconds.

speaker: John Kerry
text: The president just talked about Iraq as a center of the war on terror. Iraq was not even close to the center of the war on terror before the president invaded it.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Can I respond to that?

speaker: Moderator
text: Let’s do one of these one-minute extensions. You have 30 seconds.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Thank you, sir. First of all, what my opponent wants you to forget is that he voted to authorize the use of force and now says it’s the wrong war at the wrong time at the wrong place.

speaker: Moderator
text: Thirty seconds, Senator.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Yes, we have to be steadfast and resolved, and I am. And I will succeed for those troops, now that we’re there. We have to succeed. We can’t leave a failed Iraq. But that doesn’t mean it wasn’t a mistake of judgment to go there and take the focus off of Osama bin Laden. It was. Now, we can succeed. But I don’t believe this president can. I think we need a president who has the credibility to bring the allies back to the table and to do what’s necessary to make it so America isn’t doing this alone.

speaker: Moderator
text: We’ll come back to Iraq in a moment. But I want to come back to where I began, on homeland security. This is a two-minute new question, Senator Kerry.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Jim, let me tell you exactly what I’ll do. And there are a long list of thing. First of all, what kind of mixed message does it send when you have $500 million going over to Iraq to put police officers in the streets of Iraq, and the president is cutting the COPS program in America?

speaker: Moderator
text: Ninety-second response, Mr. President.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I don’t think we want to get to how he’s going to pay for all these promises. It’s like a huge tax gap. Anyway, that’s for another debate.

speaker: Moderator
text: Yes, let’s do a little — yes, 30 seconds.

speaker: John Kerry
text: The president just said the FBI had changed its culture. We just read on the front pages of America’s papers that there are over 100,000 hours of tapes, unlistened to. On one of those tapes may be the enemy being right the next time.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Of course we’re doing everything we can to protect America. I wake up every day thinking about how best to protect America. That’s my job.

speaker: Moderator
text: New question, Mr. President. Two minutes.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Let me first tell you that the best way for Iraq to be safe and secure is for Iraqi citizens to be trained to do the job.

speaker: Moderator
text: Ninety seconds, Senator Kerry.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Thank you, Jim.

speaker: Moderator
text: All right, go ahead. Yes, sir?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I think it’s worthy for a follow-up.

speaker: Moderator
text: Sure, right.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: My opponent says help is on the way, but what kind of message does it say to our troops in harm’s way, “wrong war, wrong place, wrong time”? Not a message a commander in chief gives, or this is a “great diversion.”

speaker: Moderator
text: Senator Kerry, 30 seconds.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Well, you know, when I talked about the $87 billion, I made a mistake in how I talk about the war. But the president made a mistake in invading Iraq. Which is worse?

speaker: Moderator
text: All right, new question. Two minutes, Senator Kerry.

speaker: John Kerry
text: No, and they don’t have to, providing we have the leadership that we put — that I’m offering.

speaker: Moderator
text: Ninety seconds.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: That’s totally absurd. Of course, the U.N. was invited in. And we support the U.N. efforts there. They pulled out after Sergio de Mello got killed. But they’re now back in helping with elections.

speaker: Moderator
text: 30 seconds, Senator.

speaker: John Kerry
text: The United Nations, Kofi Annan offered help after Baghdad fell. And we never picked him up on that and did what was necessary to transfer authority and to transfer reconstruction. It was always American-run.

speaker: Moderator
text: Thirty seconds, Mr. President.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Well, actually, he forgot Poland. And now there’s 30 nations involved, standing side by side with our American troops.

speaker: Moderator
text: New question, Mr. President, two minutes. You have said there was a, quote, “miscalculation,” of what the conditions would be in post-war Iraq. What was the miscalculation, and how did it happen?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: No, what I said was that, because we achieved such a rapid victory, more of the Saddam loyalists were around. I mean, we thought we’d whip more of them going in.

speaker: Moderator
text: Ninety seconds, Senator Kerry.

speaker: John Kerry
text: What I think troubles a lot of people in our country is that the president has just sort of described one kind of mistake. But what he has said is that, even knowing there were no weapons of mass destruction, even knowing there was no imminent threat, even knowing there was no connection with Al Qaida, he would still have done everything the same way. Those are his words.

speaker: Moderator
text: New question. Senator Kerry, two minutes. You just — you’ve repeatedly accused President Bush — not here tonight, but elsewhere before — of not telling the truth about Iraq, essentially of lying to the American people about Iraq. Give us some examples of what you consider to be his not telling the truth.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Well, I’ve never, ever used the harshest word, as you did just then. And I try not to. I’ve been — but I’ll nevertheless tell you that I think he has not been candid with the American people. And I’ll tell you exactly how.

speaker: Moderator
text: Ninety seconds, Mr. President.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: My opponent just said something amazing. He said Osama bin Laden uses the invasion of Iraq as an excuse to spread hatred for America. Osama bin Laden isn’t going to determine how we defend ourselves.

speaker: Moderator
text: Thirty seconds. We’ll do a 30 second here.

speaker: John Kerry
text: I wasn’t misleading when I said he was a threat. Nor was I misleading on the day that the president decided to go to war when I said that he had made a mistake in not building strong alliances and that I would have preferred that he did more diplomacy.

speaker: Moderator
text: Thirty seconds, Mr. President.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The only thing consistent about my opponent’s position is that he’s been inconsistent. He changes positions. And you cannot change positions in this war on terror if you expect to win.

speaker: Moderator
text: New question, Mr. President. Two minutes.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: You know, every life is precious. Every life matters. You know, my hardest — the hardest part of the job is to know that I committed the troops in harm’s way and then do the best I can to provide comfort for the loved ones who lost a son or a daughter or a husband or wife.

speaker: Moderator
text: Senator, 90 seconds.

speaker: John Kerry
text: I understand what the president is talking about, because I know what it means to lose people in combat. And the question, is it worth the cost, reminds me of my own thinking when I came back from fighting in that war.

speaker: Moderator
text: All right, sir, go ahead. Thirty seconds.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Yes, I understand what it means to the commander in chief. And if I were to ever say, “This is the wrong war at the wrong time at the wrong place,” the troops would wonder, how can I follow this guy?

speaker: Moderator
text: Senator Kerry, you have 30 seconds. You have 30 seconds, right. And then the president.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Secretary of State Colin Powell told this president the Pottery Barn rule: If you break it, you fix it.

speaker: Moderator
text: Speaking of your plan, new question, Senator Kerry. Two minutes.

speaker: John Kerry
text: The time line that I’ve set out — and again, I want to correct the president, because he’s misled again this evening on what I’ve said. I didn’t say I would bring troops out in six months. I said, if we do the things that I’ve set out and we are successful, we could begin to draw the troops down in six months.

speaker: Moderator
text: Ninety seconds.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: There are 100,000 troops trained, police, guard, special units, border patrol. There’s going to be 125,000 trained by the end of this year. Yes, we’re getting the job done. It’s hard work. Everybody knows it’s hard work, because there’s a determined enemy that’s trying to defeat us.

speaker: Moderator
text: Thirty seconds.

speaker: John Kerry
text: I couldn’t agree more that the Iraqis want to be free and that they could be free.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Yes, let me…

speaker: Moderator
text: Yes, 30 seconds.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The reason why Prime Minister Allawi said they’re coming across the border is because he recognizes that this is a central part of the war on terror. They’re fighting us because they’re fighting freedom.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. President, new question. Two minutes. Does the Iraq experience make it more likely or less likely that you would take the United States into another preemptive military action?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I would hope I never have to. I understand how hard it is to commit troops. Never wanted to commit troops. When I was running — when we had the debate in 2000, never dreamt I’d be doing that.

speaker: Moderator
text: Senator Kerry, 90 seconds.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Jim, the president just said something extraordinarily revealing and frankly very important in this debate. In answer to your question about Iraq and sending people into Iraq, he just said, “The enemy attacked us.”

speaker: Moderator
text: Thirty seconds.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: First of all, of course I know Osama bin Laden attacked us. I know that.

speaker: Moderator
text: Thirty seconds, Senator.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Thirty-five to forty countries in the world had a greater capability of making weapons at the moment the president invaded than Saddam Hussein. And while he’s been diverted, with 9 out of 10 active duty divisions of our Army, either going to Iraq, coming back from Iraq, or getting ready to go, North Korea’s gotten nuclear weapons and the world is more dangerous. Iran is moving toward nuclear weapons and the world is more dangerous. Darfur has a genocide.

speaker: Moderator
text: New question. Two minutes, Senator Kerry.

speaker: Moderator
text: Ninety seconds.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Let me — I’m not exactly sure what you mean, “passes the global test,” you take preemptive action if you pass a global test.

speaker: Moderator
text: New question, Mr. President. Do you believe that diplomacy and sanctions can resolve the nuclear problems with North Korea and Iran? Take them in any order you would like.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: North Korea, first, I do. Let me say — I certainly hope so. Before I was sworn in, the policy of this government was to have bilateral negotiations with North Korea.

speaker: Moderator
text: Senator Kerry, 90 seconds.

speaker: John Kerry
text: With respect to Iran, the British, French, and Germans were the ones who initiated an effort without the United States, regrettably, to begin to try to move to curb the nuclear possibilities in Iran. I believe we could have done better. I think the United States should have offered the opportunity to provide the nuclear fuel, test them, see whether or not they were actually looking for it for peaceful purposes. If they weren’t willing to work a deal, then we could have put sanctions together. The president did nothing.

speaker: Moderator
text: I want to make sure — yes, sir — but in this one minute, I want to make sure that we understand — the people watching understand the differences between the two of you on this.

speaker: Moderator
text: And you’re willing to do it…

speaker: John Kerry
text: Both. I want bilateral talks which put all of the issues, from the armistice of 1952, the economic issues, the human rights issues, the artillery disposal issues, the DMZ issues and the nuclear issues on the table.

speaker: Moderator
text: And you’re opposed to that. Right?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: The minute we have bilateral talks, the six-party talks will unwind. That’s exactly what Kim Jong Il wants. And by the way, the breach on the agreement was not through plutonium. The breach on the agreement is highly enriched uranium. That’s what we caught him doing. That’s where he was breaking the agreement.

speaker: Moderator
text: New question, two minutes.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Well, I’ll tell you exactly why not, but I first want to say something about those sanctions on Iran.

speaker: Moderator
text: Ninety seconds.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Back to Iran, just for a second.

speaker: Moderator
text: New question, President Bush. Clearly, as we have heard, major policy differences between the two of you. Are there also underlying character issues that you believe, that you believe are serious enough to deny Senator Kerry the job as commander in chief of the United States?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: That’s a loaded question. Well, first of all, I admire Senator Kerry’s service to our country. I admire the fact that he is a great dad. I appreciate the fact that his daughters have been so kind to my daughters in what has been a pretty hard experience for, I guess, young girls, seeing their dads out there campaigning.

speaker: Moderator
text: Ninety second response, Senator.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Well, first of all, I appreciate enormously the personal comments the president just made. And I share them with him. I think only if you’re doing this — and he’s done it more than I have in terms of the presidency — can you begin to get a sense of what it means to your families. And it’s tough. And so I acknowledge that his daughters — I’ve watched them.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I’m trying to put a leash on them.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Well, I know. I’ve learned not to do that.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Thank you.

speaker: John Kerry
text: … and a great first lady.

speaker: Moderator
text: Thirty seconds.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Well, I think — listen, I fully agree that one should shift tactics, and we will, in Iraq. Our commanders have got all the flexibility to do what is necessary to succeed.

speaker: Moderator
text: Thirty seconds.

speaker: John Kerry
text: I have no intention of wilting. I’ve never wilted in my life. And I’ve never wavered in my life.

speaker: Moderator
text: New question, two minutes, Senator Kerry.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Nuclear proliferation. Nuclear proliferation. There’s some 600-plus tons of unsecured material still in the former Soviet Union and Russia. At the rate that the president is currently securing it, it’ll take 13 years to get it.

speaker: Moderator
text: Ninety seconds, Mr. President.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Actually, we’ve increased funding for dealing with nuclear proliferation about 35 percent since I’ve been the president. Secondly, we’ve set up what’s called the — well, first of all, I agree with my opponent that the biggest threat facing this country is weapons of mass destruction in the hands of a terrorist network. And that’s why proliferation is one of the centerpieces of a multi-prong strategy to make the country safer.

speaker: Moderator
text: Just for this one-minute discussion here, just for whatever seconds it takes: So it’s correct to say, that if somebody is listening to this, that both of you agree, if you’re reelected, Mr. President, and if you are elected, the single most serious threat you believe, both of you believe, is nuclear proliferation?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: In the hands of a terrorist enemy.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Weapons of mass destruction, nuclear proliferation.

speaker: Moderator
text: Your response to that?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Again, I can’t tell you how big a mistake I think that is, to have bilateral talks with North Korea. It’s precisely what Kim Jong Il wants. It will cause the six-party talks to evaporate. It will mean that China no longer is involved in convincing, along with us, for Kim Jong Il to get rid of his weapons. It’s a big mistake to do that.

speaker: Moderator
text: All right. Mr. President, this is the last question. And two minutes. It’s a new subject — new question, and it has to do with President Putin and Russia. Did you misjudge him or are you — do you feel that what he is doing in the name of antiterrorism by changing some democratic processes is OK?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: No, I don’t think it’s OK, and said so publicly. I think that there needs to be checks and balances in a democracy, and made that very clear that by consolidating power in the central government, he’s sending a signal to the Western world and United States that perhaps he doesn’t believe in checks and balances, and I told him that.

speaker: Moderator
text: Ninety seconds, Senator Kerry.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Well, let me just say quickly that I’ve had an extraordinary experience of watching up close and personal that transition in Russia, because I was there right after the transformation. And I was probably one of the first senators, along with Senator Bob Smith of New Hampshire, a former senator, to go down into the KGB underneath Treblinka Square and see reams of files with names in them.

speaker: Moderator
text: Thirty seconds, Mr. President.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: You know my opinion on North Korea. I can’t say it any more plainly.

speaker: Moderator
text: Well, but when he used the word “truth” again…

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Pardon me?

speaker: Moderator
text: … talking about the truth of the matter. He used the word “truth” again. Did that raise any hackles with you?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Oh, I’m a pretty calm guy. I don’t take it personally.

speaker: Moderator
text: OK. All right.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: You know, we looked at the same intelligence and came to the same conclusion: that Saddam Hussein was a grave threat.

speaker: John Kerry
text: It was a threat. That’s not the issue. The issue is what you do about it.

speaker: Moderator
text: All right, that brings us to closing statements.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Thank you, Jim, very much.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. President, two minutes.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Thank you very much tonight, Jim. Senator.

speaker: Moderator
text: And that ends tonight’s debate. A reminder, the second presidential debate will be a week from tomorrow, October 8th, from Washington University in St. Louis. Charles Gibson of ABC News will moderate a town hall-type event. Then, on October 13th, from Arizona State University in Tempe, Bob Schieffer of CBS News will moderate an exchange on domestic policy that will be similar in format to tonight’s.
